reviews.title: Fix the glitches please :(
reviews.text:
Ruzzle has been my favorite mobile game for years. I started playing when I was 13 years old, and now I'm 26. Out of all the games I've downloaded and deleted over the years, this is one of the very few that has stayed on my phone.

The game is fun, brain-stimulating, and surprisingly challenging, especially when you enter tournaments and compete against strong players. It keeps your mind active, improves your vocabulary, and never really gets old. Whether I have a few minutes to spare or want to sit down and seriously compete, Ruzzle is always my go-to game.

The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because of the constant freezing and glitches. Sometimes the tiles start shaking uncontrollably across the board. I can still swipe and create words, but I can't clearly see what I'm spelling. The only way I know if a word was accepted is by listening for the approval sound. It's incredibly frustrating, especially when I'm having a great round and pushing 1,800+ points. I've had to force-close and restart the app more times than I can count because of this issue.

I genuinely love this game and have been loyal to it for over a decade. I just wish the developers would address these performance issues so the gameplay experience can match how great the game itself

reviews.title: The Gameplay is Still Good- The Rentless Sales Pitches are NOT
reviews.text:
I’ve played Ruzzle for more than 10 years. I watched it grow, recommended it to countless friends, built a team, and happily adapted to the many changes along the way. Yes, it was addictive—and that was part of its charm.
Unfortunately, the developers seem to have confused improving the game with monetizing every corner of it.
It started subtly with changes to scoring and point accumulation. Then came the endless opportunities to buy coins. Now we’re bombarded with constant pop-up ads pushing “special bundles” and promotions. Frankly, it’s become intrusive and incredibly annoying.
I paid for an ad-free experience. To me, “ad-free” should include not being repeatedly interrupted by advertisements from the developers themselves.
After more than a decade of loyalty, and after convincing many others to join me on Ruzzle, I never thought I’d say this—but I’m seriously considering deleting the app. The gameplay is still good; the relentless sales pitches are not.
What a shame. Ruzzle had something special, but greed has slowly chipped away at the experience that made players stay in the first place.






⭐⭐☆☆☆
